payload.rebuttal: fixed: Added test_a_mutator_restores_before_a_clean_interrupt_propagates in tests/test_mutation.py, driving the real host_mutator/_mutated directly with a clean file (no corruption or deletion) and a KeyboardInterrupt raised inside the with block, then asserting the file is back to its original bytes. Added the analogous test_a_clean_interrupt_still_restores_through_the_real_mutator in tests/test_witness_gate.py, doing the same through witness_gate(mutate=host_mutator(tmp_path), ...). Both close exactly the gap the critic named: every prior interrupt test corrupted or deleted the file first, and the spy in test_an_interrupt_still_propagates_through_the_new_seam used a hand-written context manager rather than saffron.mutation's real code, so neither proved restore_mutant was actually invoked on a clean interrupt. I verified the fix is real, not claimed: I applied the critic's exact suggested defect locally to saffron/mutation.py's _mutated (except BaseException: raise before the restore attempt, moving restore out of the finally) and re-ran the suite — the two new tests failed with 'left mutated by a clean interrupt', while all other tests (including the two pre-existing interrupt tests, which corrupt/delete first and so never called restore_mutant either way) kept passing. I then restored saffron/mutation.py to its committed state (confirmed via a clean git diff on that file) and committed only the two new test files.
